audit_findings.title: Redeemable minority interest is an omitted cash-settled claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.5 million purchase price; 216,994 shares issued, equal to 0.49% of the 44.69999 million valuation shares; $0.59 per valuation share equivalent
audit_findings.mechanism: The former claim affects the equity bridge and share denominator, while acquiring the remaining interest increases the common shareholders' share of Devil Mountain earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The Operating Agreement contains put and call options whereby the remaining 25 % ownership interest in Devil Mountain may be sold to the Company through the exercise of the holders’ put option or purchased by the Company through the exercise of the Company’s call option.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates that the put was exercised and settled on June 1, 2026 with treasury shares, not cash, and SiteOne now owns 100% of Devil Mountain. Therefore no redeemable claim remained at the valuation date. The issued shares are less than 0.5% of the valuation denominator, and the $26.5 million transaction value is only 0.9% of the $2,865 million base equity value. That scale cannot change the conclusion that $64.10 base value is well below the $100.58 market price. Direction is mixed because omitted dilution would overstate value, whereas failing to recognize the acquired minority earnings would understate it.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the 216,994 issued shares are included in the 44.69999 million fully diluted denominator and that projected OE reflects 100% ownership only from June 1, 2026 onward; no bridge deduction should remain.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease fleet replacement may escape owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 finance-lease principal payments of $32.5 million, new finance-lease liabilities of $38.1 million, and finance-lease ROU amortization of $35.0 million; respectively 16.4%, 19.3%, and 17.7% of the $197.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease ROU amortization is added back in operating cash flow while principal payments and noncash fleet additions are outside cash capital expenditure, recurring fleet replacement is omitted from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Our finance leases consist primarily of leases for our vehicle fleet.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates recurring, substantial fleet financing: $32.5 million of principal was paid while $38.1 million of new finance-lease obligations were incurred in 2025. The record does not establish whether the anchor contains an equivalent replacement charge, but the filed amounts are large relative to OE and could materially reduce every scenario if omitted.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $197.7 million anchor line by line to finance-lease ROU amortization, principal payments, noncash additions, and lease interest; rerun all scenarios with a normalized fleet-replacement deduction if no equivalent charge is already included, avoiding double counting interest.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may omit its acquisition cost
audit_findings.magnitude: Acquisition cash outlays were $192.7 million in 2023, $138.2 million in 2024, and $37.9 million in 2025, averaging $122.9 million annually or 62.2% of the $197.7 million anchor; acquisitions supplied $110.7 million of 2025 sales growth while Organic Daily Sales grew 1%
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition spending sits outside maintenance capital expenditure and OE, but acquisition-derived earnings can enter the historical anchor and acquisition-dependent growth can enter the 3% and 6% forecasts.
audit_findings.evidence: Our historical growth has been driven in part by acquisitions, and future acquisitions are an important element of our business strategy.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation applies 3% base and 6% bull growth without a stated acquisition funding charge. The filings show that acquisitions are integral to strategy and supplied most reported 2025 sales growth, while organic growth was only 1%. The record does not prove how much long-run growth must be purchased, but historical outlays are sufficiently large relative to OE that treating acquisition-dependent growth as free could materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Separate historical and forecast OE growth into organic and acquired components; rerun the base and bull cases either with supportable organic-only growth or with normalized acquisition, integration, and contingent-consideration outlays required to achieve each growth rate.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may be operating liquidity rather than surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $87.4 million maximum disputed bridge amount, equal to $1.96 per share and 3.1% of the $2,865 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for seasonal working capital should remain in operations rather than be added separately in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our business is characterized by a relatively high level of reported working capital, the effects of which can be compounded by changes in prices.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing supports the possibility that some June cash is operating liquidity: inventory and receivables were seasonally elevated and $124.1 million was drawn on the ABL facility. Nevertheless, even treating all $87.4 million as required cash would reduce base value only from $64.10 to approximately $62.14 per share, leaving it far below the $100.58 market price and not changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum operating cash from monthly seasonal balances and borrowing patterns and add only excess cash in the next rerun; no immediate conclusion-changing rerun is required.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring liability-release gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.9 million pre-tax and approximately $1.47 million after tax at the filed 22.5% effective rate, equal to 0.74% of the $197.7 million anchor; approximately $0.46 per share of base value if fully capitalized proportionally
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in 2025 OE, the nonrecurring other-income gain raises the anchor and is projected and capitalized as recurring earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 28, 2025, the Company recognized approximately $ 1.9 million in Other income, reflecting the release of its previously recorded environmental liability, net of the related indemnification asset.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $1.9 million nonrecurring liability-release gain, but the record does not establish whether it survived the OE reconciliation. Even if the entire estimated after-tax amount remained, its scale is less than 1% of anchor OE and approximately $0.46 per share of base value, insufficient to alter the conclusion relative to the $36.48 gap between base value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $1.9 million gain and related noncash cash-flow adjustment through the 2025 OE calculation; remove the after-tax gain if present while retaining the actual $0.5 million settlement cash payment in the appropriate period.
